QUOTE: "The code notifies the callback and then sets `approved = true` without reading any return value. Without a callback, unlisted tools are denied. With one, every call passes approval."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer states the callback is not a gate and that approved is set to true unconditionally after notifying it, ignoring any return value (it also says "(line 172, unconditional)"), which covers the cannot-refuse mechanism. It does not literally say "returns void", but the point about no return value being read carries the substance.
